seo.description: Rebuilt a multi-agency Shopify store for an arts & crafts brand — catalog restructuring, metafield-driven content, market-specific pricing, and Amazon-style rich content. Case study by Victoria Fine.

seo.ogTitle: Arts & Crafts Storefront Rebuild — Shopify Case Study
seo.ogDescription: Rebuilt a patchwork multi-agency Shopify store into a self-maintainable storefront with proper catalog architecture and market-specific pricing.

overview: ARTLINE is an international European arts-and-crafts brand shipping worldwide. I designed the new storefront (artline-resin.eu) in Figma and implemented it with a development team, architecting it so the client's own team could maintain it going forward without depending on outside developers for routine changes. The entire content and pricing model runs on metafields and metaobjects, including market-specific pricing: VAT-inclusive for Europe, VAT-exclusive elsewhere.
challenge: The client's storefront had been running since 2022, incrementally patched by a rotating cast of agencies with no consistent architecture behind it. The result was a flat product catalog that couldn't represent variants properly, a browsing experience that wasn't built to convert, and no way for customers to filter products or calculate how much material they'd actually need. That friction pushed people to abandon before checkout on a site where confidence in quantity and fit matters most.
solutionIntro: The rebuild started with the foundation the old site never had, then moved through catalog restructuring, product cards, pricing architecture, content, and editability.

solutionBlocks.text: The old storefront had no design system: every button used different styling, fonts varied inconsistently across pages, and there was no shared set of components to build from. I built a design system in Figma and implemented it as CSS custom properties for color, typography, and spacing, so every component inherits from the same tokens instead of being styled one-off. That foundation is what made it possible for the client's own team to later extend the site without breaking consistency.

solutionBlocks.alt: Design system: colors, typography, spacing, radius, and shadows

solutionBlocks.text: The old catalog listed every color and size as a separate standalone product: 276 SKUs with no shared variant structure, no way to filter by color or size, and inventory tracked separately for what should have been one product. Editing that by hand in Shopify wasn't realistic at that scale, so I exported the full catalog into Airtable via Airpower, consolidated the flat listings into proper product-variant groups, filled in the missing attributes, and synced the restructured catalog back to Shopify.

solutionBlocks.alt: Airtable PIM with restructured products and variants

solutionBlocks.text: Product cards needed to represent different kinds of product choices: some vary by color, others by physical form, others carry no meaningful visual variant. Three card templates — pill selectors, color swatches, and image-based variants — let each product type use the selection UI that matches how a customer actually chooses it. Each template is fully responsive across desktop, tablet, and mobile. Customers can also add a product to cart directly from the catalog grid, selecting a variant and adding it without opening the product page.

solutionBlocks.alt: Product card templates: pill selectors, color swatches, and image variants with add-to-cart from catalog

solutionBlocks.text: Product pages include modular rich-content blocks: applications, step-by-step usage instructions, specifications, and cross-sell pairings, built the way Amazon A+ content is structured, since the same content needed to serve both the Shopify storefront and Amazon listings. Every block is built from metaobjects, so content is entered once and renders consistently across sections instead of being hand-coded per product.

solutionBlocks.alt: Product page with modular rich content: applications, how to use, specifications, and cross-sell pairings
